goal_text: Improve Top 25% performance while maintaining or improving underdog performance
diagnostics_summary: Iteration 3: Removed stale monotonic constraints (set to 0) for 3 features removed in iteration 1. Result: catastrophic underdog collapse. ROI dropped 70% (0.33 to 0.10), accuracy -3.52%, +250_plus odds band imploded (47.1% to 22.2% accuracy, 0.92 to -0.16 ROI). Top 25% improved substantially (+5.48%) and Top 10% (+3.34%), but this came at unacceptable cost to underdogs. Model became more extreme: higher confidence on top predictions but worse broad performance. Lesson: Even 'stale' constraints set to 0 influence model behavior and prevent features from contributing unconstrained.

previous_iteration_result.summary: Removing stale monotonic constraints caused catastrophic underdog performance collapse: ROI -70%, accuracy -3.52%, +250_plus odds band imploded. Top 25% improved +5.48% but insufficient to offset underdog damage.
previous_iteration_result.key_learning: Even constraints set to 0 prevent features from influencing predictions. Removing them allows unconstrained learning, which can catastrophically harm underdog calibration. Keep stale constraints at 0 to disable features without removing them from the schema.

avoid_constraints: Do NOT remove features (learned from iteration 1)
Do NOT remove monotonic constraints, even if stale (learned from iteration 3)
Do NOT add new features involving quality differences
Underdog performance must NOT degrade significantly (>2%)
Underdog ROI must NOT drop more than 10%
strategy_pivot: Abandon constraint manipulation. Focus exclusively on regularization hyperparameters (lambda, min_child_weight, max_depth, subsample, colsample_bytree) to reduce overfitting and improve Top 25% while preserving underdog performance. The model's 8% train-validation gap suggests regularization is the right approach, but must be done more carefully.
hypotheses: Moderate lambda increase (1.5 to 3.0, not higher) will reduce overfitting and improve Top 25% without harming underdogs
Increasing min_child_weight (3 to 5) prevents overfitting on small samples while maintaining feature interactions
Combining small regularization adjustments (lambda + min_child_weight) will be more effective than large single changes
Reducing max_depth (6 to 5) limits complexity while preserving most feature interactions
The 3 constrained features should remain at 0 to prevent unconstrained learning that harms underdogs
Sampling-based regularization (subsample, colsample_bytree) reduces variance without removing features

proposed_iterations.focus: Restore monotone_constraints.json with 3 removed features at 0 constraint
proposed_iterations.rationale: Iteration 3 removed constraints for num_common_opponents, orthodox_vs_orthodox, southpaw_vs_southpaw, causing catastrophic underdog collapse. This iteration restores those constraints at 0 to disable the features while keeping them in the schema. This should restore baseline performance and allow further iterations to proceed with stable configuration.

Current lambda (1.5) may be too low, causing overfitting. Increasing to 2.5 will penalize large leaf weights and reduce the 8% train-validation gap. This moderate increase should improve Top 25% validation accuracy without harming underdogs, avoiding the aggressive changes that caused issues in iteration 3.

Higher min_child_weight prevents leaves with few samples, reducing overfitting. Increasing from 3 to 5 will improve generalization by requiring more samples in each leaf. This should improve Top 25% accuracy while preserving feature interactions that underdogs depend on.

Current max_depth of 6 may allow too much complexity. Reducing to 5 will limit interaction depth, reducing overfitting while preserving most feature interactions. This moderate reduction should improve Top 25% validation performance without the catastrophic effects seen in iteration 3.

Current subsample and colsample_bytree are both 1.0 (no sampling). Reducing both to 0.85 adds stochastic regularization, preventing the model from memorizing specific patterns. This sampling-based approach should improve Top 25% generalization by reducing variance without removing features.

If iterations 5 and 6 individually show promise but insufficient improvement, combining them may have additive effects. Moderate increases to both lambda and min_child_weight together will reduce overfitting through multiple mechanisms without aggressive changes that harm underdogs.

If regularization approaches improve Top 25% but underdogs still struggle in +150 to +250 band (44.4% accuracy), add a targeted feature capturing underdog momentum specifically for mid-range odds. This feature will help the model identify live underdogs without removing existing features or disrupting high-confidence predictions.
